Add your SOTA logs

Upload instructions and supported log combinations

Choose or drop one or more SOTA V2 CSV exports in the area above. Activator, S2S and chaser files are identified automatically. You can add files together or separately, with one file of each type. Adding another file of the same type replaces it.

  • Any log alone: convert its contacts.
  • Activator + S2S: enrich matching activator contacts with worked-summit information. Unmatched S2S contacts are reported and not added.
  • Activator + chaser or S2S + chaser: enrich matching contacts and add chaser contacts absent from the other log.
  • All three: enrich the activator log with S2S information, then merge the chaser log.

Matching records are combined without duplicate contacts. Ambiguous matches and conflicting summit references are reported without guessing. Chaser-only contacts have no own summit or locator; these fields are omitted.

Optional. Leave blank to include the whole log. The chosen date is inclusive; contact dates are UTC. Invalid CSV rows are still reported.

Summit enrichment

Fetch summit locators directly from the SOTA API. Successful summit lookups are cached on this device for 24 hours. Only summit references are sent; your log stays here.

Additional callsign exports

Review and select each mapping. Preserve overseas locations: EA/G1ABC/P → EA/G1ABC. For G1ABC/EA/P, enter G1ABC/EA instead of G1ABC. Unselected callsigns stay separate. Original exports are always retained.

These additional files repeat contacts in the original exports. Import one set per destination to avoid duplicates. Contacts already logged under the destination callsign are excluded from the additional file.

Load a log with slash-separated station callsigns to review mappings.

Summit locators
Own-summit locators are required. Worked-summit locators are optional; leave them blank if unknown. Enter a Maidenhead locator, such as IO81XW, then convert again.
    

    ⌁ Built for the summit-to-logbook journeyNo uploads. No account. No installation.
    

    DATA mode compatibility
    SOTA DATA contacts are exported unchanged as MODE=DATA for TQSL use. DATA is not a standard ADIF mode, so other logging programs may reject these contacts or require you to correct their mode before importing.
    

    About this browser edition
    Based on SOTAtoADIF by Jack G5JDA. Supports the original project's implemented activator workflow. Chaser logs are supported; contacts without an own summit omit own summit and locator fields. Optional S2S CSV imports enrich matching activator contacts, or can be converted alone. Existing S2S data in an activator CSV is retained with corrected SOTA_REF fields. Rows without a valid band, mode, date, or station locator are excluded and reported. Times are treated as UTC.
    For LoTW/TQSL usage, read the original guidance and check station locations before importing. Conversion is local; optional live enrichment requires internet access. You can disable it and enter summit locators manually.
